27 OCT 2026 / DATA DIAGNOSIS

Getting the perspective right.

The 100k-position CSV stored scores from the side to move. The C++ loader expected White’s perspective before its own conversion. Earlier conversion instructions therefore reversed Black-to-move targets.

The fix belonged in the converter. Changing both sides would have applied the correction twice.

Read the experiment log ↗
NEXT SCALE / 100M POSITIONS

More data. A new checkpoint.

The v1 documentation records a 10-epoch CUDA run on 100 million Lichess evaluated positions. Epoch 10 was selected as the best float model before quantization.

145.1062 cpValidation MAE · float model

63,930.4994 cp² validation MSE. Validation error measures prediction accuracy; it is not an Elo rating or a playing-strength result.

03 / UNDER THE HOOD

The work behind
the best move.

The current engine keeps search, legal moves, and incremental evaluation in C++. NNUE accumulators update during make/unmake, with rebuilds when king buckets change.

Explore the native engine ↗
Search that remembers

A bounded transposition table, principal variation search, killer moves, and quiet-move history help organize the search. Quiescence covers check evasions, captures, and promotions.

Checks beyond the opening position

Tests compare incremental and fresh scores for castling, en passant, promotions, and king moves. UCI integration checks cover legal moves, timing, stop, node limits, mate, and game-over positions.

Known boundaries

Standard chess only; one search worker. No pondering, Chess960, opening book, or tablebases. There is no measured playing rating. The custom KFQ1 network format does not accept Stockfish networks.

RUN THE CURRENT ENGINE

Your next move.

Requires Python with venv/pip, Make, and a C++17 compiler. First setup downloads and verifies the trained network. See the engine README for Lichess integration.

TERMINAL
git clone https://github.com/crazykitten43/kittenfishv1.git
cd kittenfishv1
./scripts/setup.sh
./kittenfish
